tldr.text: Northslope came to you: an inbound discovery call driven by a document-heavy construction-defect lawsuit.
Legal Ops is your champion and wants document visibility; the GC backs the goal but is skeptical her lean team can run review in-house.
Outside counsel is in the room and has a revenue reason to resist — treat that as the meeting's main landmine.

note.text: Joined about 8 months ago and runs a lean team; supportive of the goal but wants to see it, not hear it — and she is the likely economic buyer.
Submitted the demo request and drove both calls — your internal champion, frustrated by how much of the matter is handled externally.
Added to this call late; his firm currently runs — and bills for — the ediscovery workflow you would help bring in-house.

dealState.text: Early stage: the opportunity sits in Discovery, opened as an inbound demo request shortly after the defect lawsuit reached the trade press.
One prior 20-minute intro call has happened; today is the first working discovery session.
They are actively evaluating: the champion viewed the AI-review and pricing pages the day after confirming this call.

lastConversation.text: The champion called the defect matter 'a document monster' — years of change orders, RFIs, and subcontractor email.
The GC's objection was bandwidth, not value: she is 'not sure we can bring this in-house' with a team of four.
Sentiment was neutral-to-positive, and the rep committed to resend the defect-dispute case study.

whyNow.text: Northslope is newly named in a multi-party construction-defect suit over the St. Aubin hospital expansion — a document-discovery phase is coming.
The completed hospital build left an enormous documentation footprint across dozens of trades — the exact volume that breaks manual review.

buriedAlpha.text: Your 'skeptic' has done this before. The GC joined about 8 months ago from Vantage Grid Energy, and on the intro call she let slip that at her last company they ran a big investigation on a review platform — she has seen the upside firsthand, which makes her far more winnable than her caution suggests.

hypothesizedPains.pain: Rising litigation cost with no visibility into their own documents.

rationale.text: The GC says litigation work goes straight to outside counsel and the board is asking pointed questions about the budget.

hypothesizedPains.pain: A four-person legal team cannot review the document volume by hand.

rationale.text: The champion wants to 'look at our own documents,' but the matter spans years of project records and the team is already stretched.

hypothesizedPains.pain: They want review in-house but doubt they can stand it up.

rationale.text: The GC is open to it yet fears buying 'a thing that sits on a shelf' because no one has time to deploy it.

proofPoints.title: A general contractor took defect review in-house (Cascade Ridge)

note.text: Closest analog you have: a regional GC in a multi-party defect dispute ran first-pass review in-house with a single paralegal and cut review time by roughly 55%.

proofPoints.title: Early Case Assessment maps the matter before review

note.text: ECA shows custodians and where change-order activity clusters — a direct answer to the champion's 'visibility' ask.

proofPoints.title: AI-Assisted Review makes a small team viable

note.text: It lets one skilled paralegal, with attorney oversight, do what previously needed an outside team — speaking straight to the bandwidth objection.

askThese.question: Walk me through how the St. Aubin documents are handled today — who touches them, and where do they live?

rationale.text: You already know outside counsel's vendor runs it and the team can't even see the platform; confirm the workflow in their words.

askThese.question: If review came in-house, who would actually operate it day-to-day?

rationale.text: The champion named the paralegal, Tina, as the operator and wants her to see it — get her into the next session.

askThese.question: What has to be true for you to feel confident this won't become a second job for your team?

rationale.text: This is the GC's whole ballgame — she said proof it won't burden her team is what she needs to see.

askThese.question: How does a tooling decision like this usually get evaluated and approved on your side?

rationale.text: You have no budget or procurement-authority data yet; this opens the topic without applying pressure.

landmines.title: Outside counsel is in the room

guidance.text: Gregory Hale's firm bills for the current setup, so he is not a neutral voice on changing it. Don't pitch replacing them — frame ReadyRoom as making them faster and more transparent.

landmines.title: Don't oversell — the GC wants the boring version

guidance.text: She explicitly asked to see 'the boring parts' and what her paralegal's Tuesday looks like. A flashy demo will backfire with her.

unknowns.text: Their budget for this is unknown — no figure has been shared, and the opportunity amount on file is an internal estimate, not a customer number.
We don't know who holds procurement authority or how a purchase gets approved on their side.
We don't have the size of the document set (custodians, data volume) — the champion said he would try to get a real figure before this call.
